[b]The Domus of Alexander, Dining Hall:  March 5th, 2025[/b]

The vote had gone poorly, someone had pulled a last minute coalition, and the two most powerful parties had managed to force the Chamber of the Peoples to vote against an investigation of Tito Alexandrii-Claudis. Alexander now stewed, at a low lying dining table, laying on a couch, he and his closest allies in the Senate and Chamber of the Peoples, Edwin Ettes, Thyron Targin a representative of a midlands region, and lastly Col. Severus Albin of the national defense force.

The vote today was a miserable affair, that last minute coalition, I find it suspect, began Alexander.

That it was Alexander, and I can tell you that I saw that Consantin, he was smiling after that vote like a child who has been given candy, replied Thyron.

Was he really? Enquired Alexander, That is quite mad, he stated lazily, Someone shouldve punched him, he smirked.

I wouldve, replied Edwin bluntly, popping a date into his mouth.

I heard a rumor, began Thyron, That the Lady Ptoleny was seen at the basilica today, he continued.

Was she? Enquired the colonel.

Yes, in fact she was, stated Alexander brushing a strand of blonde hair out of his face, She visited me, made a deal, apparently her husband wants to replace Tito, continued Alexander.

Is that so? Stated Edwin in surprise, I knew there was meddling by them in the senate, but not at this level, he continued.

Oh yes my dear friend, they meddle and peddle around in all affairs, it is why Doma is the chief justice and Tito the speaker, there of this can be no doubt, stated Alexander.

And what did you say to her offer, you rejected it I hope, replied Thyron.

I did, to her face, I dont think she liked it, replied Alexander.

Womans probably never been told no in her life, muttered the colonel.

Aye to that, replied Edwin raising his glass to the colonel, chuckling slightly.

Joking aside, stated Alexander, How do we recover? What ground do we still have? He enquired rising slightly to observe his compatriots.

Well, given the results of these two votes, the one in the Senate and the one in the Chamber both going in favor of an already unpopular president, there will most certainly be a public uproar, began Thyron.

Yes, of course, stated Alexander, But uproar is not enough, we need action, he continued, looking at the colonel who was staring into his glass, Colonel? He enquired.

Ah yes! Replied the colonel, slightly surprised at being approached, Yes, action, he stated numbly, Well with the people outraged as you have stated, it is possible to perhaps cause a brighter fire to burn, through calculated disturbances, he stated.

Precisely, replied Alexander, For instance, with protests the army is almost always called out, or at least the army police, he stated, if the protestors are perhaps pushed a certain way, the police will react, if they are pushed to react violently, then.. he stated, his voice trailing off.

Then the state comes under scrutiny for allowing violence, replied Ettes almost leaping up, My dear Alexander you are brilliant! He cried.

But wait! Stated Thyron, What if the bait is not taken, what if suspicions are raised, we must consider the fallout,  he said.

Perhaps we do not need to raise an uprising, replied
 the colonel thoughtfully, You see, the president is due to give a speech in a week, to both chambers, there will already be a military presence, and of course protestors, he continued.

All we need is a spark, replied Alexander grinning wickedly. 

I have some contacts in the protesting world, stated Ettes, Small contacts, but they have connections, who have connections to larger more well financially endowed groups, he continued.

Then get them, we must be ready by next week, stated Alexander, furrowing his brow slightly.

My dear friends, shall we toast to our victory? enquired Thyron.

Yes of course, a toast! replied Alexander excitedly.

A toast to victory, a toast to the republic, a toast to democracy, declared the colonel, raising his glass, followed by the rest. 

The plan had been laid, now all that was left was the process of ensuring success. Though Alexander held a tinge of fear in his mind as he recalled the warning that Theodora had made to him about his family.
